findings.problem: OrderWorkflow uses raw String for status and separate bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of an enum typestate, making illegal states representable — e.g. status='sent' with is_sent=false, or is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None.
findings.failure_mode: Business invariants are not enforced by the type system; callers can construct or mutate workflows into inconsistent states that violate order-domain rules.
findings.fix: Replace status String + is_validated bool + is_sent bool + sent_at_epoch_ms Option with a single OrderStatus enum typestate (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) that encodes the lifecycle. Use a constructor or fallible builder to prevent illegal transitions.

findings.problem: OrderWorkflow.id is a raw String with no domain semantics or invariants encoded in its type.
findings.failure_mode: Any String can be assigned as an order ID, allowing duplicates, empty strings, malformed IDs, or cross-domain confusion.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype `OrderId(String)` with a private field and a fallible constructor that enforces domain invariants (non-empty, valid format).

findings.problem: OrderWorkflow.status is a raw String instead of a domain enum. Combined with separate bool flags, this duplicates state the compiler cannot check.
findings.failure_mode: Status string can drift out of sync with is_validated/is_sent booleans, creating unreachable or contradictory state combinations that runtime code must manually guard against.
findings.fix: Replace status String with an `OrderStatus` enum typestate that fully describes the lifecycle stage. Remove is_validated and is_sent as redundant fields.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates OrderWorkflow in-place with raw field assignments instead of a pure transition function that returns a new valid state or an error. No validation of preconditions (e.g. order must be validated before sent).
findings.failure_mode: Orders can be marked sent without ever being validated, bypassing domain invariants. No error type for invalid transitions — failures are silent state corruption.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to a pure function `fn mark_sent(state: OrderStatus) -> Result<OrderStatus, TransitionError>` that enforces the state machine (e.g. only Validated -> Sent) and returns a typed domain error for invalid transitions.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a new String via to_string() every time mark_sent is called, even though the string literal is known and fixed.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation on every transition; in hot paths this degrades performance. The String type for status also prevents compile-time state encoding.
findings.fix: Eliminate status field entirely via typestate enum. If a display name is needed, use enum::as_str() which returns &'static str with zero allocation.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an Option<u64> that is decoupled from the is_sent flag. When is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms should be Some, but the type system cannot enforce this coupling.
findings.failure_mode: An order can be marked sent without a timestamp (is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=None), making audit trails incomplete and timestamp-based queries unreliable.
findings.fix: Encode the timestamp as part of the typestate — e.g. `OrderStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }` — so the timestamp is required and type-safe when the order is in the sent state.

findings.problem: OrderWorkflow is a plain public struct with all pub fields. Any code can construct it with arbitrary values, bypassing all domain invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Callers outside the module can create OrderWorkflow instances with any combination of status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms, including logically impossible states.
findings.fix: Make fields private and provide a constructor or builder that enforces invariants. Better yet, replace the struct with a typestate enum that makes illegal states unrepresentable.

findings.problem: No functional core / imperative shell separation is visible. The OrderWorkflow struct and mark_sent function mix data model with state transition logic without a clear pure core.
findings.failure_mode: State transitions cannot be tested in isolation from I/O side effects; domain logic is tangled with structural representation.
findings.fix: Define pure domain types (OrderId, OrderStatus enum) and pure transition functions in a core module. Shell code handles persistence, serialization, or I/O separately.

residual_risk: The order workflow typestate is entirely missing — status is a String and lifecycle is encoded in three decoupled fields. This allows any illegal state combination to exist at runtime with no compile-time guard. mark_sent has no precondition checks and silently corrupts state. Without enum typestates, fallible constructors, and pure transition functions, the domain invariants are purely documentation-level. Static review only; no commands run.
